==Problem==

In <imath>\bigtriangleup ABC</imath>, <imath>AB=BC=29</imath>, and <imath>AC=42</imath>. What is the area of <imath>\bigtriangleup ABC</imath>?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }100\qquad\textbf{(B) }420\qquad\textbf{(C) }500\qquad\textbf{(D) }609\qquad \textbf{(E) }701</imath>

==Solution 1==
We know the semi-perimeter of <imath>\triangle ABC</imath> is <imath>\frac{29+29+42}{2}=50</imath>. Next, we use Heron's Formula to find that the area of the triangle is just <imath>\sqrt{50(50-29)^2(50-42)}=\sqrt{50 \cdot 21^2 \cdot 8}=\boxed{\textbf{(B) }420}</imath>.

==Solution 2 (easier)==
Splitting the isosceles triangle in half, we get a right triangle with hypotenuse <imath>29</imath> and leg <imath>21</imath>. Using the Pythagorean Theorem , we know the height is <imath>\sqrt{29^2-21^2}=20</imath>. Now that we know the height, the area is
<imath>\dfrac{(20)(42)}{2} = \boxed{\textbf{(B)}~420}</imath>.
